title: Nobody Blockaded Hormuz to Slow India-Europe Trade. The Corridor Meant to Bypass It Is Getting Built Faster Anyway.

version_history.note: Publish new post: Hormuz blockade / IMEC / India-EU FTA piece. Corrects the premise that the 2026 US naval blockade of Iran was a reaction to India-Asia-Europe trade integration (the India-EU FTA was concluded a month before the war began; analyst literature treats IMEC as something the war exposed, not something it targeted). Documents real freight-cost impact on Gulf-adjacent India-Europe trade, draws a historical parallel to VOC/EIC ship seizures and blockades (Amboyna 1623, Battle of Masulipatnam 1673) and Operation Earnest Will (1987-88), and traces the longer Pax Britannica-to-Pax Americana 'freedom of the seas' throughline including the postcolonial critique of that doctrine. Closes with a factual, clearly-labelled-as-editorial aside on 2026's prize-law tanker seizures and the Trump commemorative coin.
